rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or evaluator feedback, so this is a conservative baseline meant to finish the course and produce telemetry. Geometry: five line sensors spaced 10 mm apart across x = +/-20 mm (sensor_size 12 mm, which covers the 25 mm tape with margin), all at y = 30 mm ahead of the axle so they read the line before the wheels reach it. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a stable, moderately agile base. Body width 0.12 m keeps the off-track limit at max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.0425 m... the larger of 0.06 m and the tape-based limit, so about 0.06 m of tolerance. Mass 0.8 kg with body length 0.18 m gives moderate yaw inertia. Controller: the signal is a reading-weighted average of weights [1.0, 0.5, 0, -0.5, -1.0] (positive = left), so it is proportional to lateral error and bounded by 1. kp = 3.0 gives a full-scale turn of about 3 (about 1050 PWM differential) at the edge of the line, which is strong enough to track bends without saturating. kd = 0.05 damps the response slightly, and ki = 0 avoids integral windup on the long bends. base_speed = 1.6 (PWM about 80 percent) targets an average speed near 1.5 m/s to finish inside 3 s. line_loss = last_direction, so the robot turns back toward the side it last saw the line. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with some oscillation on the slalom. The measurements requested (rms_error, max_error, steering_oscillation, line_loss_events, completion_time) will show whether kp is too high (oscillation, large max_error) or too low (large rms_error on the bends) and whether speed is limiting completion time. Hypotheses to test next: (1) if steering_oscillation is high, reduce kp and raise kd; (2) if completion_time is near 3 s with progress below 1, raise base_speed; (3) if line_loss_events is above 0, widen the sensor span or add a sensor.
